stages.title: Language sounds and pronunciation
stages.hook: Russian has sounds that English does not have. Can you hear which part of a word is said loudest?
explain: Every Russian word has one stressed syllable. It is said longer and louder. In молоко (moloko) the stress is on the last part: молокО.
Vowels that are not stressed get weaker. In молоко the first two о letters sound like a short "a": it sounds like "malako". So learn each new word together with its stress.
stages.mnemonic: Stress is the drum beat of a Russian word: loud on one beat, soft on the others.

gq.q: How is the first о in молоко (stressed on the last syllable) pronounced?
gq.why: An unstressed о is weakened and sounds like "a": "malako".

gq.q: How is the letter х in хорошо pronounced?
o: A rough breathy sound, like "ch" in Scottish "loch"
gq.why: Russian х is a rough "kh" sound made in the back of the mouth.

panel.q: Why can reading a Russian word "as it is spelled" give a wrong sound?
o: Russian has silent consonants in every word
Unstressed vowels are weakened, so the sound can differ from the letter
Russian letters change sound every day
panel.why: Vowel reduction means о often sounds like "a" when unstressed, so you must know the stress.

panel.q: The words замок (castle) and замок (lock) are spelled the same. What tells them apart?
o: The number of syllables it has
panel.why: ЗАмок is a castle and замОк is a lock: stress can change meaning.

panel.q: In хлеб (bread) the final б sounds like "p". What does this show?
o: The letter б is silent at the end of every Russian word in speech
A voiced consonant at the end of a word is said unvoiced
panel.why: Final devoicing: хлеб is said "khlyep".

teach.model: Each Russian word has one stressed syllable that is louder and longer. Other vowels are weaker, and о is said like a short "a" when unstressed, as in молоко. Stress can even change meaning, so learn it with every new word.

points.ask: What do you mean by stress?
What happens to the other vowels?
Can you give me an example word?

trip.prompt: Find the part about vowel reduction and write down one word where о sounds like "a".

stages.title: Alphabet, script or basic characters
stages.hook: The Russian letter Р looks like English P, but it sounds different. Can you guess its sound?
explain: Russian uses the Cyrillic alphabet with 33 letters. Some letters look like English ones and sound the same, like К and М. Others are "false friends": В sounds like v, Н sounds like n, Р sounds like a rolled r and С sounds like s.
Some letters are new, like Д (d), Б (b), Г (g) and Я (ya). Two letters, Ь and Ъ, have no sound of their own. They only change how the letters beside them are said.
stages.mnemonic: False friends: В says v, Н says n, Р says r, С says s. They only pretend to be English.
sentences: Here are a cat and a house.

gq.q: Which sound does the Russian letter Р stand for?
gq.why: Р looks like P but is the Russian r, trilled with the tip of the tongue.

gq.q: How many letters are there in the Russian alphabet?
gq.why: The Russian alphabet has 33 letters, including Ь and Ъ.

panel.q: The alphabet is called Cyrillic. Why?
o: It was invented by a Russian tsar called Cyril
It is linked to Saint Cyril and the Slavic mission he led with his brother Methodius
panel.why: Cyrillic is named in honour of Cyril, who with Methodius worked among the Slavs; it was shaped by their followers from Greek letters.

panel.q: Why is it risky to read Н as "h" and С as "k"?
o: They are silent letters in the middle of words
Russian has no n or s
They are false friends: Н is n and С is s
panel.why: Look-alike letters carry different sounds, so check each letter instead of guessing from English.

panel.q: The letters Ь and Ъ do not make a sound. What do they do?
o: They signal softness or a separation of nearby sounds
They mean the word is plural
panel.why: The soft sign softens a consonant and the hard sign separates it from the next vowel.

teach.model: Russian uses 33 Cyrillic letters. Some look like English letters but sound different, so В is v, Н is n, Р is r and С is s. Two letters, Ь and Ъ, make no sound alone.

points.ask: How many letters are there and what is the alphabet called?
Do the letters sound like English ones?
Are there letters with no sound?

trip.prompt: Look at the table of letters and find three letters that look like English ones but sound different.

stages.title: Greetings and introductions
stages.hook: When do you say Привет to a friend, and when do you say Здравствуйте?
explain: Привет (privet) means "hi" and is for friends and family. Здравствуйте (ZDRAST-vuy-tye) is "hello" for teachers, shop staff and anyone you do not know well. The first в is not pronounced.
To say your name, say Меня зовут (menya zovut), which means "they call me". To ask a friend, say Как тебя зовут? To ask an adult stranger, use the polite form: Как вас зовут?
stages.mnemonic: Ты is for your team, Вы is for the boss: small word, big respect.

gq.q: You meet your new teacher. Which greeting is best?
gq.why: Здравствуйте is the polite greeting for teachers and people you do not know well.

gq.q: You ask an older stranger for their name. Which question is polite?
gq.why: Вас is the polite "you", used with strangers and elders.

panel.q: In Здравствуйте the first в is not pronounced. What does that teach us?
o: Russian never uses the letter в in the middle of any word
The word is borrowed from French
The letter в is a vowel
Russian spelling does not always show the sound exactly
panel.why: Some consonant clusters are simplified in speech: it sounds like "ZDRAST-vuy-tye".

panel.q: Why do Russians have two words for "you", ты and вы?
o: Вы is both plural and polite, and ты is informal singular
They are two spellings of one word
panel.why: Choosing ты or вы shows the relationship between speakers.

panel.q: You greet a friend in a text. Which is the natural choice?
panel.why: Привет is casual and fits a friend. Goodbye or very formal phrases would sound odd.

teach.model: Use Привет with friends and Здравствуйте with teachers or strangers. To give your name say Меня зовут and your name. Ask Как тебя зовут? to a friend and Как вас зовут? politely.

points.ask: How do I say hello?
How do I say my name?
When do I use the polite form?

trip.prompt: Find how greetings change with politeness and note one example from another language.

stages.title: Numbers and counting
stages.hook: In Russian, "two cats" and "five cats" use different endings for "cat". Why?
explain: Count from one to eight: один, два, три, четыре, пять, шесть, семь, восемь. Then comes девять (9) and десять (10).

The noun changes after a number. After один we use the basic form: один кот. After два, три, четыре we use a special form: два кота. From five on we use another form: пять котов. Also один has genders: один дом, одна мама, одно окно.
stages.mnemonic: One cat, two cat-A, five cat-OV: the number tells the ending.

gq.why: After два, три and четыре the noun takes a special form, here кота.
Один has the feminine form одна with feminine nouns.

panel.q: Why is it пять котов but два кота?
o: The noun form depends on the number: 2 to 4 take one form and 5 or more take another
Two is a plural and five is a singular
It is only a spelling habit
panel.why: Numbers 2-4 govern the genitive singular, and 5 and above the genitive plural.

panel.q: Мне пять лет means "I am five years old". What does it show about how Russians state age?
o: The verb "to be" is understood and used in the past tense
The person is in the dative: literally "to me five years"
Age is written in Roman numerals
panel.why: Russian uses мне (to me) and a number, with no verb "to be".

panel.q: What happens to один when the noun is neuter, as in окно?
panel.why: Один agrees in gender: один, одна, одно.

teach.model: The numbers are один, два, три, четыре, пять, шесть, семь, восемь. The noun after the number changes: один кот, два кота, пять котов. Один also has the forms одна and одно.

points.ask: What are the first numbers?
Does the word for the thing change?
What about one with different words?

trip.prompt: Find the numbers one to ten and say them aloud twice.

stages.title: Colours and shapes
stages.hook: Russian has two different basic words for blue. Why do you think that is?
explain: Colour words are adjectives, so they must agree with the noun: красный мяч (a red ball, masculine), красная машина (a red car, feminine), красное яблоко (a red apple, neuter).

Russian has two basic blues: синий is dark blue and голубой is light blue, like the sky. Shapes are круг (circle), квадрат (square), треугольник (triangle). The letter ё has two dots and is always stressed.
stages.mnemonic: Red ball, red car, red apple: красный, красная, красное. The ending follows the noun.
sentences: The snow is white and cold.

gq.q: Which is correct for "a red apple" (яблоко is neuter)?
gq.why: The adjective agrees with the neuter noun, so it ends in -ое.
Голубой is light blue; синий is dark blue.

panel.q: Why does Russian have two words for blue?
o: It treats light blue and dark blue as two basic colours
The two words mean the same
panel.why: Languages divide the colour space differently, and Russian treats light and dark blue as separate basic colours.

panel.q: What is special about the letter ё?
o: It is always silent and never changes the sound of the word
It is used only for foreign names
It is always stressed, though it is often printed as е
It makes the previous letter soft only in writing
panel.why: Ё is stressed; ordinary texts often write е, so learners should learn the words with ё.

panel.q: "Красная машина" — why is красная used?
o: Машина is feminine, so the adjective takes the feminine ending
panel.why: Adjectives match the gender of their noun.

teach.model: Colours are adjectives and agree with the noun: красный мяч, красная машина, красное яблоко. Russian has two blues, синий for dark and голубой for light.

points.ask: Does the colour word change?
Is there anything special about blue?
Can you give me an example?

trip.prompt: Look for the Russian blues in the page and think why two words might matter.

stages.title: Family and people
stages.hook: Who is a бабушка and who is a дедушка? Think of the people who tell you stories.
explain: The words for family are: мама, папа, брат, сестра, бабушка (grandmother), дедушка (grandfather) and семья (family). Друг is a friend.

The word "my" changes with the noun: мой брат, моя сестра, моё имя. To say "I have a brother" Russians say У меня есть брат, which is literally "by me there is a brother". Russians also have a middle name from the father, such as Иванович, called отчество.
stages.mnemonic: Мама and папа are the same in many languages. Моя goes with feminine words, мой with masculine.

gq.why: Сестра is feminine, so "my" is моя.

gq.q: What is the отчество in Anna Ivanovna Petrova?
o: Anna, her first name and her father's name
Ivanovna, formed from her father's name
gq.why: The patronymic is made from the father's first name, here Ivan.

panel.q: Why does Russian say У меня есть брат instead of "I have a brother"?
o: It uses a "by me there is" structure and has no ordinary verb "to have" here
panel.why: Possession is expressed with у plus the person and есть.

panel.q: A teacher is called Мария Ивановна. Why use both names?
o: It is only used with children
Name plus patronymic is a respectful way to address someone
panel.why: Using the first name and patronymic is polite and common at school and work.

panel.q: Why do мама and папа look similar in many languages?
o: Early baby sounds often form words for parents
They were copied from English into all other languages
panel.why: Simple syllables like ma and pa are among the first sounds babies make.

teach.model: Use мама, папа, брат, сестра, бабушка and дедушка. My changes by gender: мой брат, моя сестра. Say У меня есть брат for "I have a brother".

points.ask: What are some family words?
How do I say "my"?
How do I say I have a brother?

trip.prompt: Find what a patronymic is and make one for a made-up person.

stages.title: Common objects
stages.hook: There is no word for "a" or "the" in Russian. How does a book stay "a book"?
explain: Russian has no articles. Книга can mean "a book" or "the book". Every noun has a gender. Most masculine nouns end in a consonant (стол), feminine in -а or -я (книга) and neuter in -о or -е (окно).
The word "is" is not used in the present: Это книга means "This is a book". To ask where something is, say Где? (where), as in Где мой телефон? Use на стол-е to say "on the table".
stages.mnemonic: Стол is a boy, книга is a girl, окно is a thing in between.
sentences: The book lies on the table.

gq.q: Which of these nouns is neuter?
gq.why: Nouns ending in -о are usually neuter.

gq.q: How do you say "a book" in Russian?
gq.why: Russian has no articles, so книга means both "a book" and "the book"; один would be "one", and it would also need the feminine form одна.

panel.q: Why is it Это моя книга but not "это есть моя книга"?
o: Russian has no verb for "to be" in any tense at all
Есть is only used with food
Russian omits the present tense of "to be"
panel.why: In the present, the verb "to be" is left out, so Это моя книга is the natural sentence.

panel.q: A learner says "мой окно". What is wrong?
o: Окно is neuter, so it should be моё окно
Окно is feminine, so it should be моя окно
panel.why: The possessive agrees with the noun gender: моё for neuter.

panel.q: Why does стол become столе in "на столе"?
o: Because стол is plural in this sentence and takes a plural ending
The noun takes the prepositional case after на for location
Because it ends with a vowel
It is an irregular word with no pattern
panel.why: Russian nouns change their ending according to their role, here the prepositional case for position.

teach.model: Russian has no a or the. Every noun is masculine, feminine or neuter, which you can often tell from the ending. Say Это книга for "This is a book" without a verb.

points.ask: Does Russian have a and the?
What is gender?
How do I say "This is a book"?

trip.prompt: Find how many genders Russian has and give one example of each.

stages.title: Everyday actions
stages.hook: How does the Russian verb change when I read, you read and the children read?
explain: Russian verbs have endings that show who does the action. For читать (to read): я читаю, ты читаешь, он читает, мы читаем, вы читаете, они читают.

Other useful verbs are писать (to write), играть (to play), спать (to sleep), пить (to drink), есть (to eat) and говорить (to speak). Because the ending shows the person, Russians often drop the pronoun and say Читаю книгу.
stages.mnemonic: Я читаЮ, ты читаЕШЬ: the end tells the person.
sentences: The children play in the yard.

gq.why: The он ending for this verb is -ает.

gq.q: How do you say "I am a student" in the present?
gq.why: The present tense of "to be" is omitted.

panel.q: Why can Russian say just Читаю книгу without я?
o: The verb ending already shows the person
Russian has no personal pronouns in speech
panel.why: The ending -ю can only go with я, so the pronoun is optional.

panel.q: Why is "они играют" different from "он играет"?
o: The verb agrees with the subject in person and number
It is just a spelling change
panel.why: Они is plural, so the verb takes the plural ending -ют.

panel.q: In Я читаю книгу, why is it книгу and not книга?
o: Книгу is the plural form used after a verb of reading
The direct object takes the accusative ending
The verb changes the noun to feminine
panel.why: Книга is the dictionary form; as the object of читаю it becomes книгу.

teach.model: Russian verbs change their endings with the person: я читаю, ты читаешь, он читает. Because the ending shows who acts, the pronoun can be dropped.

points.ask: Do verbs change?
Can you show me an example?
Do I need to say я?

trip.prompt: Find the table of present-tense endings and compare two persons.

stages.title: Simple listening and speaking
stages.hook: What would you say if you hear Russian and do not understand?
explain: Useful phrases when you listen: Я не понимаю (I do not understand), Повторите, пожалуйста (Please repeat), Говорите медленно (Speak slowly). To say you understand, say Я понимаю.

Как дела? means "How are things?" and a normal reply is Хорошо, спасибо. In Russian, a yes/no question may have the same words as a statement but the voice goes up on the key word. Ты говоришь по-русски? means "Do you speak Russian?"
stages.mnemonic: Listen, repeat, slow down: three tools that make talking possible.

gq.why: Как дела? asks how you are, so a short answer about how you are fits.

gq.q: How does a spoken yes/no question usually differ from a statement in Russian?
o: Verbs change to a special question form
The voice rises on the key word
gq.why: Intonation turns the same words into a question.

panel.q: You do not catch a sentence. Which request is polite to a stranger?
panel.why: Using the polite plural form with пожалуйста is appropriate with strangers.

panel.q: Why do Russians sometimes say Как дела? and expect a short answer?
o: It is only used for doctors and their patients
It works as a greeting as well as a question
panel.why: Like English "How are you?", it is often a social ritual.

panel.q: Why practise saying phrases aloud as well as reading them?
o: Stress and intonation are part of meaning and do not show in spelling
panel.why: Pronunciation, stress and intonation need speaking practice.

teach.topic: Getting help when you do not understand
teach.model: Say Я не понимаю if you do not understand. Ask Повторите, пожалуйста for repetition and Говорите медленно for slower speech. Reply to Как дела? with Хорошо, спасибо.

points.ask: How do I say I do not understand?
How do I ask someone to say it again?
How do I ask for slower speech?

trip.prompt: Find a short audio sample or phrase list and repeat two lines aloud.
